elements.before: Veterinary Practice & Animal Hospital Feasibility & Market Studies

Independent, lender-grade analysis for veterinary practices and animal hospitals financed through SBA 7(a) and 504, USDA rural, conventional practice-finance, and net-lease capital. A veterinary practice is a going concern, cash flow and equipment plus heavy professional goodwill, not passive real estate. This page is our standing read on where the market is feasible, how ramp-up and production forecasts fail review, and the difference between the market study, the feasibility study, and the going-concern appraisal a lender requires.
elements.after: A practice is a going concern whose value is mostly professional goodwill, so a veterinary feasibility study tests DVM staffing, production and the ramp. Feasibility Study Company prepares veterinary practice and animal hospital feasibility studies for veterinarians buying or building a practice, for developers, and for their lenders; its market study covers the pet households in reach. The Census Bureau counted 34,296 veterinary practices in 2023,1 and lenders weigh each new one, or each sale, under SBA 7(a) and 504, USDA rural, practice-finance and net-lease programs.
